claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the current record, based primarily on aggregate readiness passing, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and planned monitoring, despite an unresolved 1.5-point gap in a named regulated-customer use case and an open legal review on disclosure.
decision_criteria: Audit the claim that the model can be certified now.
Require admissible evidence for each policy predicate, not business rationale alone.
Treat named contractual or launch use cases as material under the stated policy.
Do not treat low-volume or non-core labels as resolving materiality when customer commitments or legal review are present.
Public governance guidance can support process quality, but cannot substitute for required internal disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
Absent evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance, certification is not policy-compliant.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the health-plan benefits support gap must be disclosed.
Evidence that the limitation was disclosed in the model card or other required launch documentation before certification.
Evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this named launch use case before launch.
Evidence that the 1.5-point segment gap was remediated and re-evaluated to target before certification.
Any contractual or launch-governance record clarifying whether the regulated-customer pilot order form makes this a named launch commitment.
specific_concerns: The policy states that a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; the affected segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is admissible evidence of an open legal ticket on whether this gap must be disclosed, with no final answer.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the policy predicate for an unresolved material limitation in a named use case.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring in general, but they do not override the internal disclosure policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record despite the unresolved named-use-case gap and open legal review.
That aggregate readiness plus monitoring is sufficient to satisfy the release policy without evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that the 3% projected first-month traffic figure resolves materiality for a named regulated-customer use case.
